feature_contract.goal: Prevent wrong full-target viewport skips when an R84 stereo right-eye or saved game render target is recreated at the same COM address across frames or during device loss.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only R33 per-frame target-extent metadata leases in DX9Ex independent R84; no changes to game HUD semantics, actual viewport geometry, DX11, DXVK, R26_SAFE, original input, FFB, or SkyGlow.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Source-confirmed functional hazard: R33's cached GetDesc width/height was keyed only by borrowed IDirect3DSurface9 pointer and reset only on Reset/rollback; same-pointer surface recreation in another frame could reuse wrong extents and skip a required SetViewport. This corrects a stereo state restoration and rendering safety blocker, not a measured FPS gain or proven Quest3 symptom.
trace_stages: R84 game device draws per-eye with R33TargetResetViewportMatches or R33SavedTargetResetViewportMatches after target switches; a full-target metadata cache makes ordinary per-draw SetViewport redundant.
At the native Present return or device-lost cooperative-state branch, R33 now expires both borrowed surface extent identities so an address reused during resize cannot carry its previous dimensions.

The next per-eye draw re-queries GetDesc for new target extents and skips SetViewport only if its actual current full viewport is an exact match, with normal mono/fail-closed and right-eye restore intact.
subcomponents: Invalidate both original RT0 and right-eye viewport extent leases at native frame boundary, not per draw, preserving within-frame hot-path savings.
Invalidate both target leases immediately on D3DERR_DEVICELOST or D3DERR_DEVICENOTRESET, including paths that bypass the normal Present postamble.
Add targeted negative regression for both invalidation paths and same-address resized target; retain existing viewport/stereo/restore assertions.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: R84 right-eye and game original render-target GetDesc extent validation
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Each new frame starts with invalid right-eye and original-target extent leases, re-probes current surface size once per target and elides redundant SetViewport only within the proven current-frame full-target extent.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: D3D9Ex device loss, same-address resize, and conservative original SetViewport fallback
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Both cached COM addresses expire on lost/notreset or normal Present; a 2496x2688 cached surface may not authorize a 2048x2160 recreated surface or bypass a viewport mismatch, while existing mono/restore paths stay unchanged.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Windows x86 R84 and R26_SAFE, x64 OpenXR host, package and isolation/inspector CI gates
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: All mandatory Actions complete successfully on one record-bearing exact result SHA, with runtime Quest3/VDXR left UNTESTED until physical verification.

diagnosis.root_cause: R33 cached right-eye and original target extents by borrowed COM address over multiple Present frames, clearing only on Reset or rollback; recreated same-address surfaces could be mistakenly assumed to have prior dimensions.
diagnosis.original_evidence: R33TargetResetViewportMatches and R33SavedTargetResetViewportMatches both reuse their cached width/height when surface pointer matches; PresentDestR33 previously did not clear those viewport identities after the frame, nor in device-lost fast bypass.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Both per-eye right render-target switch and original game render-target viewport restoration are protected by separate frame-local caches, and both leases expire together so a stale surface address cannot skip viewport correction.
source_trace: src/vr/d3d9/stereo_renderer_r33.cpp: R33TargetResetViewportMatches snapshots right eye GetDesc only when extent lease invalid.
src/vr/d3d9/stereo_renderer_r33.cpp: R33SavedTargetResetViewportMatches snaps original game RT0 GetDesc independently.
src/vr/d3d9/stereo_renderer_r33.cpp: PresentDestR33 now clears both caches after normal Present and in device loss bypass.
tools/verify_vr_r33_full_target_viewport.py: existing viewport restore assertions plus same-pointer reuse model and loss/normal invalidation predicates.
alternatives_rejected: Never clear on every draw: it forces two extra driver GetDesc calls on a hot path with thousands of stereo draws, regressing frame pacing; invalidate once at the actual Present/loss boundary instead.
Pointer equality cannot prove resource-generation identity across target recreation; preserve the conservative explicit SetViewport when full dimensions do not match.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Material source commit 660ce0110ae449a1fa6888b9af03b5972d561c1c changes both renderer lifecycle and same-pointer negative regression; not a HUD-only metadata change.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: verify_vr_r33_full_target_viewport.py asserts both normal Present and lost-device invalidation and models stale same-pointer 2496x2688 vs 2048x2160 mismatch, retaining existing inset/Z/restore negative tests.
diagnosis.runtime_evidence: No Quest3/VDXR or real game display test performed in this automation; visual correctness and FPS improvement not claimed.
diagnosis.next_hmd_experiment: Quest3/VDXR exact-source build: resize/recenter between portrait extents and full-screen, inspect right/left viewport edges, restored UI, road and car stereo, lens/GOAL, and track frame timing compared to control.

next_action: Run the existing required full exact-SHA DX9Ex Active, Domain, Full Source Impact and EXE HUD Inspector gates on the record-bearing successor; mark BUILD_VERIFIED only on confirmed exact-SHA success. No duplicate score or HMD PASS.
